subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` remain a supported hard-enforcement surface, and if so should Telegram adapt it into shared direct-aware tool-policy resolution rather than the current group-only path?
rationale: The schema and types already expose the surface, but the runtime does not enforce it; changing either side affects security expectations and existing operator configs.

options.title: Enforce Direct Tools
options.body: Treat the existing Telegram direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported, route direct-session policy through a shared resolver, and add regression tests for exact and wildcard DMs.

options.title: Retire The Surface
options.body: If maintainers do not want per-DM hard enforcement, remove or reject the accepted config shape through doctor/docs so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Broader Binding Policy
options.body: Leave this issue open but explicitly make #49567 the product decision for all per-binding restrictions, accepting that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct Tools
recommendation.body: Treat the existing Telegram direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported, route direct-session policy through a shared resolver, and add regression tests for exact and wildcard DMs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent maintainer-side work carried the central policy/config files on current main, and this decision spans config compatibility plus security posture.
